steps.body: A group can grow one toy at a time, and the count grows with it: six, seven, eight — counting ON from where it stood.
steps.narration: A group can grow one toy at a time, and the count grows with it: six, seven, eight — counting ON from where it stood.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 13.
14 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 10 to land on 13.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 10 and count on 3: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 3 more is 13 — counting on continues the count instead of starting over.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts are needed to reach 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 3 numbers, on 13.

predict.prompt: You know there are 12. Three more arrive. What do you do?
predict.reveal: The 12 is already counted; only the newcomers need numbers.

cml.actionGoal: Pair each object with exactly one number and trust the last number said for kch grow by one.
invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch grow by one.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more object joined the group, what would the last counting word become?

options.feedback: Correct — each counting number is exactly one more than the number before it.
15 is the number we started from, not the one that follows it.
17 skips a number; counting moves one at a time.
14 comes BEFORE 15; the count moves forward, not back.
